thread.title: Intel cloud slowdown sending stock toward worst day in six months - MarketWatch

author: Wallace Witkowski
title: Intel cloud slowdown sending stock toward worst day in six months - MarketWatch
text:
Intel Corp. was on track for its worst day in six months Friday following a sobering earnings report that showed a slowdown in cloud sales and triggered at least two downgrades.
Intel INTC, -5.52% shares dropped more than 6% in morning trading, slipping into negative territory for the year, after the Santa Clara, Calif.-based chip maker reported revenue and an outlook that fell short of Wall Street estimates late Thursday. The stock drop is the worst one-day decline since July 27, 2018, when Intel reported below-consensus data-center growth for the second quarter .
In comparison, the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +0.63% rose 1.1%, the S&P 500 SPX, +0.82% was up 0.9%, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index COMP, +1.18% advanced 1%, and the PHLX Semiconductor Index SOX, +2.12% was up 1%. For the year, both the Dow and S&P 500 are up 6.4%, the Nasdaq is up 7.8%, and the SOX index is up 9.6%.
On Friday, Susquehanna Financial analyst Christopher Rolland and Needham analyst N. Quinn Bolton both used the occasion of the earnings report to downgrade Intel to a hold rating. At least eight analysts cut their price targets on Intel while two raised targets, lowering the average price target to $53.32 from a previous $54.85.
Late Thursday, Intel reported that its two largest segments, PC-based sales and data-center sales, fell short of Wall Street expectations in the fourth quarter, and revealed that the first-quarter outlook had soured amid growing concern about trade and economic issues, especially with China. Also, Intel blamed “weaker modem demand,” most of which comes from Apple Inc.’s AAPL, +2.69% iPhones.
Read: Intel’s cloud boom is no longer making it rain, and that’s a problem
Intel said it expects adjusted earnings of 87 cents a share on revenue of about $16 billion for the first quarter, and $4.60 a share on revenue of about $71.5 billion for the year. Before the report, analysts were expecting earnings of $1 a share on revenue of $17.29 billion for the first quarter, and $4.51 a share on revenue of $73.11 billion for the full year. After changes in response to earnings, analysts on average were looking for 89 cents a share on revenue of $16.25 billion for the first quarter on Friday morning, and $4.49 a share on revenue of $71.54 billion for the year.
Needham’s Bolton downgraded Intel because of how the slowdown in cloud spending and issues with China will affected data-center, or DCG, sales.
“Both factors will severely affect DCG demand through 2Q19. Given DCG, the company’s largest growth driver, is simultaneously experiencing decelerating demand and facing tough comps over the next two to three quarters,” Bolton said.
Susquehanna’s Rolland also based his downgrade of Intel on the slowing of data-center sales.
“Management blamed the shortfall on a slowdown in China, weaker modem demand, cloud customers absorbing capacity, and a weakening NAND environment,” Rolland said. NAND chips are the flash memory chips used in USB drives and smaller devices, such as digital cameras.
“But versus our prior 1H19 estimate, Data Center is expected to drive the majority of the miss as management highlighted server inventory builds (enterprise) and ‘a period of consumption’ by cloud customers,” Rolland said.
MKM Partners analyst Ruben Roy, who has a buy rating and a $58 price target on Intel, said he believes the data-center concerns are short term.
“While it is difficult to assess the extent of slowdown, Intel does believe that server related inventory is modestly higher relative to historical levels,” Roy said. “We continue to believe that the longer-term trends in the data center remain intact and should drive profitable growth for Intel.”
In a note titled “Cloud digestion finally catches up to Intel,” Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore, who has a hold rating and a $55 price target, said the debate as to whether Intel will be impacted by macro trends and cloud weakness has already been answered by the outlook.
Read: AMD’s Lisa Su takes center stage at CES, taking aim at Intel and Nvidia
What remains to be seen, however, is how the company will manage delays in its new chip building process in the face of a competitive product from Advanced Micro Devices Inc. AMD, +3.07% and how much of a difference a new chief executive will make.
On Thursday’s call, interim CEO Bob Swan said he was “convinced” Intel’s board would “close on a new CEO in the near future.”
Of the 39 analysts who cover Intel, 18 have buy ratings, 14 have hold ratings and seven have sell ratings after Friday’s changes.
